summary.title: [1.5.4] Toy Models of Superposition & Sparse Autoencoders
summary.one_liner: Work through guided exercises on superposition in toy models, privileged bases, and training sparse autoencoders to disentangle superposed features.
keywords: how do neural networks store more features than dimensions
train a sparse autoencoder in python
takeaways: Superposition means a model represents more features than it has dimensions, using directions that interfere with each other.

Polysemanticity (one neuron, many features) is implied by superposition but is not the same thing; neurons are a privileged basis because of elementwise nonlinearities, while the residual stream is not.
Higher feature sparsity tends to produce more polysemantic neurons, since sparse features rarely interfere.
Sparse autoencoders are trained on toy superposition models, with techniques like neuron resampling and Gated or Jump ReLU architectures.
summary.summary: This ARENA chapter section is a guided, notebook-style course on superposition in transformers. It opens with recommended reading (a LessWrong post, Neel Nanda's Dynalist notes, and Anthropic's Toy Models of Superposition paper) and then covers toy models in nonprivileged and privileged bases, feature geometry, deep double descent, and sparse autoencoders. The page includes worked conceptual Q&A on privileged bases, superposition versus polysemanticity, feature importance and sparsity, and how to define a feature. The final section trains SAEs on toy models, including resampling and gated architectures; the page lists hardware needs (GPU recommended, about 11 minutes) and a Python setup using PyTorch.
